questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to measure the mass of a sample of teff?
questions.explanation: A beam balance measures mass; the others measure time, temperature and length.

questions.prompt: Which subatomic particle has almost no mass and moves around the nucleus?
questions.explanation: Electrons are very light and move around the nucleus in shells; protons and neutrons sit inside the nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which everyday substance is a base?
questions.explanation: Soap is slippery and basic (pH above 7); vinegar, lemon juice and stomach acid are all acids.

questions.prompt: Which organ system carries oxygen and food to all parts of the body?
questions.explanation: The circulatory system, with the heart and blood, transports oxygen and nutrients around the body.

questions.prompt: Mushrooms and bacteria that break down dead leaves are called:
questions.explanation: Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet, a giant made mostly of gas.

questions.prompt: A dark shadow forms behind a tree on a sunny day mainly because light:
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines, so it cannot bend around the tree, leaving a shadow behind it.

questions.prompt: Which material is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and a good conductor; wood, plastic and rubber are insulators.

questions.prompt: A square garden has sides of 5 m. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a square = side × side = 5 m × 5 m = 25 m²; area is measured in square metres.

questions.prompt: Convert 3 minutes into seconds.
questions.explanation: 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 3 × 60 = 180 seconds.

questions.prompt: An atom has 12 protons, 12 electrons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 12 + 12 = 24; electrons are too light to count.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a molecule made of two different kinds of atoms?
questions.explanation: Water (H₂O) is made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms; the others contain only one kind of atom.

questions.prompt: A gardener tests rainwater and finds it has a pH of 5. The rainwater is:
questions.explanation: A pH below 7 means acidic; pH 5 is only a little below 7, so the water is slightly acidic.

questions.prompt: Which part of the digestive system connects the mouth to the stomach?
questions.explanation: The oesophagus is the muscular tube that pushes food from the mouth down to the stomach.

questions.prompt: Which organ system protects the body and helps control its temperature?
questions.explanation: The integumentary system (skin) covers and protects the body and helps control temperature.

questions.prompt: In the food chain leaves → caterpillar → lizard → hawk, which organism is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: A herbivore eats only plants; the caterpillar eats the leaves, so it is the herbivore.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource?
questions.explanation: Wind is renewable because it is naturally replaced; coal, natural gas and iron ore can run out.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet and comes right after Earth from the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, just after Earth, and looks reddish.

questions.prompt: When water boils in a pot, hot water rises and cooler water sinks. This way of moving heat is:
questions.explanation: In liquids and gases, warm parts rise and cool parts sink, carrying heat by convection.

questions.prompt: You can see a wooden chair that gives off no light of its own because:
options: The chair makes its own light
Light from a source reflects off the chair into your eyes
Sound from the chair reaches your eyes
Heat from the chair lights it up
questions.explanation: We see non-luminous objects when light from a source bounces off them and enters our eyes.

questions.prompt: A block has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 200 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 600 g ÷ 200 cm³ = 3 g/cm³.

questions.prompt: Two atoms both have 6 protons, but one has 6 neutrons and the other has 8 neutrons. Which statement is correct?
options: They are the same element with different mass numbers
One of them is a molecule
questions.explanation: The number of protons (atomic number) decides the element, so both are the same element; different neutron numbers give different mass numbers.

questions.prompt: How many atoms are present in two molecules of ammonia, NH₃?
questions.explanation: One NH₃ molecule has 1 + 3 = 4 atoms, so two molecules have 4 × 2 = 8 atoms.

questions.prompt: Which pair of substances would react together in a neutralization reaction?
questions.explanation: Neutralization happens between an acid and a base; sulfuric acid (acid) and potassium hydroxide (base) react to give a salt and water.

questions.prompt: The inner wall of the small intestine has many tiny folds and projections. How does this help the body?
options: It increases the surface area for absorbing digested food
questions.explanation: The folds and projections increase the surface area, so more digested food can be absorbed into the blood.

questions.prompt: In a food chain, why is there always a producer at the start?
options: Producers capture energy from the Sun and bring it into the food chain
Producers have no need for energy
questions.explanation: Producers (green plants) trap energy from the Sun by photosynthesis, providing the energy that flows to all other organisms.

questions.prompt: A river is polluted and most of its fish die. What is the most likely effect on a bird that feeds only on those fish?
options: The bird will have more food
The bird will lose its food supply and may move away or die
The bird will start making its own food
The bird will turn into a producer
questions.explanation: The bird depends on the fish for food; losing them removes its food supply, so it may leave or die.

questions.prompt: If the Sun's gravity suddenly disappeared, what would happen to the planets?
options: They would stop moving at once
They would fly off in straight lines into space
They would fall into the Sun
They would spin faster in their orbits
questions.explanation: Gravity keeps planets curving in their orbits; without it they would travel off in straight lines into space.

questions.prompt: During a storm, a girl sees lightning and hears the thunder several seconds later. What does this delay tell us?
options: Sound travels much slower than light
Light needs a medium to travel
questions.explanation: The flash and bang happen together, but light reaches her almost instantly while the slower sound arrives later.

questions.prompt: In a circuit with a cell, a switch and two bulbs joined one after another, one bulb burns out. What happens to the other bulb?
options: It also goes off because the circuit is broken
questions.explanation: When bulbs are joined one after another (in series), a burnt-out bulb leaves a gap, breaking the loop so no current flows and the other bulb goes off.

questions.prompt: A student claims a liquid speeds up plant growth. Which step would BEST test this claim fairly?
options: Give the liquid to one plant and nothing to a similar plant, keeping all other conditions the same
Give the liquid to a plant kept in the dark and compare with one in sunlight
Give the liquid only once and never check the plants again
Change the soil, water and light for each plant
questions.explanation: A fair test changes only the factor being studied (the liquid) and keeps every other condition the same, using a control plant for comparison.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the structure of an atom is correct?
options: Electrons are found inside the nucleus
Protons and neutrons are found in the nucleus, and electrons move around it
questions.explanation: Protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral) make up the nucleus, while negative electrons move around it in shells.

questions.prompt: Which observation correctly identifies a base using litmus paper?
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus paper blue, while acids turn blue litmus paper red.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why both physical and chemical digestion are needed?
options: Physical digestion alone fully breaks food into molecules
Chemical digestion alone is enough without chewing
Physical digestion breaks food into small pieces so enzymes in chemical digestion can act on more surface
Neither type of digestion is really needed
questions.explanation: Chewing and churning (physical) break food into small pieces, giving enzymes (chemical) more surface to work on, so digestion is faster and more complete.

questions.prompt: Which combination of features best explains why Earth can support life but Mercury cannot?
options: Earth is the biggest planet and Mercury is the smallest
Earth has liquid water, oxygen and a suitable temperature, while Mercury lacks these
Earth makes its own light and Mercury does not
Earth has no gravity but Mercury has strong gravity
questions.explanation: Life needs liquid water, breathable oxygen and a moderate temperature; Earth has all three at the right distance from the Sun, while Mercury does not.

questions.prompt: A metal pot with a wooden handle is used for cooking. Why is the handle made of wood rather than metal?
options: Wood conducts heat better than metal
Wood is an insulator, so it stays cool and is safe to hold
Wood makes the food cook faster
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat well and would burn the hand, but wood is a poor conductor (insulator), so the handle stays cool enough to hold.
